introduction: A release is more than a tag. It includes an identifiable artifact, compatible configuration and schema, test evidence, and a recovery procedure another person can execute.

This capstone packages the complete private Taskboard stack, records its exact artifact identity, restores a saved backup into a separate database and recovers from a bad image selection. You will prove the boundaries you have learned rather than install another tool.
prerequisites: Finish unit, real-PostgreSQL integration and authenticated HTTP system tests from weeks 6–7.
Use the learner Taskboard folder and private .env with TASKBOARD_STAGE=07.
Reserve time for a clean-checkout rehearsal and restoration. Do not delete the development volume or replace its database.

concepts.title: Release identity includes more than source
paragraphs: A source commit identifies code, but the running result also depends on the image, configuration and schema. Record the local image ID now and a registry digest once you publish in the next level. A mutable tag alone is insufficient evidence.

The release dossier connects commit, base/dependency pins, migration versions, selected artifact, test results and known limitations. Your recovery procedure should select an existing tested artifact instead of rebuilding and hoping it matches.
concepts.example: The same old commit can produce a different image if an unpinned dependency changes between builds.
concepts.judgment: Use a complete evidence chain. Do not equate a familiar tag name with tested content.

concepts.title: A backup is useful only through a tested restore
paragraphs: A successful dump command proves it produced an artifact, not that the artifact restores correctly. Restore into a new database, verify counts and contents, and retain the original untouched until the result is understood.

This logical backup covers the selected database's schema and data, with ownership/grants intentionally omitted for the lab. It is not point-in-time recovery and does not establish recovery of every cluster-global object or external dependency.
concepts.example: Matching row counts can hide changed titles or owner IDs. Compare all six stored task fields in stable order.
concepts.judgment: Define what recovery must preserve, test that claim directly, and state what your backup does not cover.

concepts.title: Application rollback cannot reverse every data change
paragraphs: Replacing an app image changes executable code. It does not undelete a removed column or recover rows overwritten by a bad migration. A previous binary may be incompatible with the current schema.

Before rollback, check whether both old and new versions can use the current schema. Compatible additive changes permit more options. Destructive changes may require a forward fix or an isolated restore and a deliberate data-loss decision.
concepts.example: An old image expecting a removed title column cannot be repaired merely by changing its tag.
concepts.judgment: Treat schema compatibility as part of the release decision rather than discovering it during an incident.

steps.title: Run and record the three evidence levels
steps.purpose: Use the actual commands before wrapping them in automation.

commands.code:
cd ~/dev-opps-lab/app/taskboard
source .venv/bin/activate
mkdir -p reports
python -m pytest tests/unit tests/contract --junitxml=reports/week08-unit.xml || exit 1
docker compose up -d app
docker compose --profile test run --build --rm integration || exit 1
docker compose --profile test run --build --rm system || exit 1
explain: The local pytest command records a JUnit report for unit/adapter tests.
Compose starts the private stack. The two one-off services exercise real PostgreSQL and HTTP respectively.
Each command must exit zero. A report file's existence does not override a failing test exit.
An explicit failure branch stops the sequence instead of letting later commands run after a failed prerequisite. Correct the cause and reopen Bash if the guard closed this terminal.
commands.expected: Passing checks for all three boundaries with actual outputs retained.
commands.troubleshoot: Do not continue release approval when a required suite fails or silently skips its intended boundary.

steps.checkpoint: Record which tests ran against which application and database stage.

steps.title: Build and identify the candidate
steps.purpose: Use a clean committed source state. If git status shows intended changes, review and commit them before recording the release.

commands.code:
cd ~/dev-opps-lab/app/taskboard || exit 1
if test -f compose.week06-fault.yaml; then
  test ! -e reports/week06-fault.yaml || { printf '%s\n' 'Inspect the existing archived fault before moving another copy.'; exit 1; }
  mv -- compose.week06-fault.yaml reports/week06-fault.yaml || exit 1
fi
git add .gitignore .dockerignore .env.example Dockerfile compose.yaml pytest.ini requirements.lock requirements-dev.lock reference starter migrations tests tools ci README.md
git diff --cached --stat
git diff --cached --check
explain: Work in the copied application. Move only the deliberately created week-6 override into ignored evidence, after refusing to overwrite an older copy.
git add stages the named intended application inputs, excluding credentials, reports and the local venv. Inspect the staged list and whitespace check before running the next block.
An explicit failure branch stops the sequence instead of letting later commands run after a failed prerequisite. Correct the cause and reopen Bash if the guard closed this terminal.
commands.expected: Only intended application inputs are staged; no .env, backup, venv or generated report is included.
commands.troubleshoot: If unrelated work is already staged in the parent learner repository, inspect and unstage it deliberately before making this release commit.

commands.code:
if ! git diff --cached --quiet; then git commit -m 'Record the reviewed week 8 application release' || exit 1; fi
git status --short
test -z "$(git status --porcelain --untracked-files=normal -- .)" || { printf '%s\n' 'Review and commit intended application inputs; archive temporary faults under ignored reports before building.'; exit 1; }
git rev-parse HEAD > reports/week08-commit.txt
docker build --target runtime --build-arg GIT_SHA="$(git rev-parse HEAD)" -t devopps-taskboard:week08 . || exit 1
docker image inspect devopps-taskboard:week08 --format '{{.Id}}' > reports/week08-image-id.txt || exit 1
GOOD_IMAGE=$(cat reports/week08-image-id.txt)
TASKBOARD_IMAGE="$GOOD_IMAGE" docker compose up -d --no-build app
TASKBOARD_IMAGE="$GOOD_IMAGE" docker compose --profile test run --rm system || exit 1
curl --fail --show-error http://127.0.0.1:8000/version
explain: git status reveals uncommitted inputs; rev-parse records the exact commit.
build packages runtime with that commit as version metadata. image inspect records the actual local image ID.
The command-local TASKBOARD_IMAGE value selects that artifact without editing .env. --no-build forbids rebuilding during selection.
The system suite checks the candidate actually running; /version connects its metadata to the recorded commit.
Commit the reviewed staged inputs if needed. The explicit clean-application guard stops a build whose source would differ from its recorded commit; it includes untracked files within this app folder.
An explicit failure branch stops the sequence instead of letting later commands run after a failed prerequisite. Correct the cause and reopen Bash if the guard closed this terminal.
commands.expected: The tested runtime is the recorded local image ID and reports the intended commit.
commands.troubleshoot: If Compose cannot select a local image ID in your installed engine, use the week08 tag and verify its resolved ID equals the saved ID before proceeding; do not claim a registry digest that has not been pushed.

steps.checkpoint: Write the release identity, migration versions and remaining private-lab limitations.

steps.title: Restore the saved backup into a separate destination
steps.purpose: Pause other writers while creating and comparing the snapshot. Include at least one incomplete and one completed task from the prior system tests.

commands.code:
mkdir -p reports
docker compose exec -T db pg_dump -U taskboard -d taskboard --format=custom --no-owner --no-privileges > reports/week08.dump || exit 1
RESTORE_DB=taskboard_restore_$(python -c "from uuid import uuid4; print(uuid4().hex[:12])")
printf '%s\n' "$RESTORE_DB" > reports/week08-restore-name.txt
docker compose exec -T db createdb -U taskboard "$RESTORE_DB" || exit 1
docker compose exec -T db pg_restore -U taskboard -d "$RESTORE_DB" --exit-on-error --no-owner --no-privileges < reports/week08.dump || exit 1
explain: mkdir prepares reports. exec -T avoids a pseudo-terminal corrupting the binary dump. pg_dump creates a custom-format logical backup; redirection writes its bytes to a file.
The UUID suffix creates a fresh destination name and records it. createdb must succeed for this new destination; never reuse the source name.
pg_restore reads the saved dump from stdin, stops on error, and does not attempt to restore ownership/grant statements. Source taskboard remains untouched.
An explicit failure branch stops the sequence instead of letting later commands run after a failed prerequisite. Correct the cause and reopen Bash if the guard closed this terminal.
commands.expected: A nonempty dump and a new independent restored database.
commands.troubleshoot: Pause task writers before the snapshot/comparison. On dump/restore error, stop and inspect it; do not overwrite a working database to simplify recovery.

commands.code:
RESTORE_DB=$(cat reports/week08-restore-name.txt) || exit 1
python -c "import re,sys; sys.exit(0 if re.fullmatch(r'taskboard_restore_[0-9a-f]{12}', sys.argv[1]) else 1)" "$RESTORE_DB" || { printf '%s\n' 'Refused an invalid disposable restore database name.'; exit 1; }
QUERY='COPY (SELECT id,owner_id,title,completed,created_at,completed_at FROM tasks ORDER BY id) TO STDOUT WITH CSV HEADER'
docker compose exec -T db psql -U taskboard -d taskboard -c "$QUERY" > reports/week08-source.csv || exit 1
docker compose exec -T db psql -U taskboard -d "$RESTORE_DB" -c "$QUERY" > reports/week08-restored.csv || exit 1
diff -u reports/week08-source.csv reports/week08-restored.csv
explain: Read the actual saved destination and validate its exact disposable-name pattern before using it.
QUERY selects all six stored fields in stable ID order. COPY emits CSV including a header; each psql command writes one comparison file.
diff -u prints differences and exits nonzero if content differs. A silent zero exit means these snapshots match.
Validation uses an explicit exit code and the shell stops on failure, so a failed name check cannot fall through into a query or dropdb. It also remains active under Python optimization.
An explicit failure branch stops the sequence instead of letting later commands run after a failed prerequisite. Correct the cause and reopen Bash if the guard closed this terminal.
commands.expected: No differences for a nonempty stable task dataset.
commands.troubleshoot: If writers changed the source after backup, the comparison is invalid as a snapshot-equality test. Quiesce the lab and repeat with a fresh named destination; do not dismiss unexplained differences.

steps.checkpoint: Keep the dump, restored destination name and complete comparison evidence. Explain why matching count alone was insufficient.

failure.title: Select an image name that does not exist
failure.boundary: This changes only the selected image for one command. It may fail before replacing the healthy container; observe actual state rather than claiming an outage.

explain: A command-local variable supplies a bad image tag. --no-build prevents a fallback build and --pull never prevents a registry lookup.
inject.expected: A missing-image failure. Existing container behavior must be inspected separately.
inject.troubleshoot: If that tag happens to exist locally, select a verified absent lab tag; do not remove unrelated images.

investigate.code:
docker compose ps
curl --include --max-time 5 http://127.0.0.1:8000/version
cat reports/week08-image-id.txt
explain: ps and the HTTP read establish whether the previous service remained available.
The saved image ID identifies the tested recovery artifact independent of a movable tag.
investigate.expected: A clear record of deployment failure versus actual availability, plus the known-good artifact ID.
investigate.troubleshoot: A failed deployment command alone does not prove users saw downtime.

hints: Separate 'new release did not start' from 'old service stopped'.
Recovery should not invoke docker build.

explanation: The selection points to no local artifact. Re-select the recorded tested image and verify behavior. Avoid rebuilding an old commit as a substitute for identifying the previous artifact.

recover.code:
GOOD_IMAGE=$(cat reports/week08-image-id.txt)
TASKBOARD_IMAGE="$GOOD_IMAGE" docker compose up -d --no-build app
explain: Load the previously recorded image ID and select it for this controlled deployment without a build.
recover.troubleshoot: Review current schema compatibility before applying this pattern to later migrations.

verification.code:
TASKBOARD_IMAGE="$GOOD_IMAGE" docker compose --profile test run --rm system || exit 1
curl --fail --show-error http://127.0.0.1:8000/version
explain: Run the business contract checks and compare version metadata after recovery.
An explicit failure branch stops the sequence instead of letting later commands run after a failed prerequisite. Correct the cause and reopen Bash if the guard closed this terminal.
verification.expected: The same intended artifact passes system checks.
verification.troubleshoot: A healthy liveness endpoint alone is not sufficient recovery evidence.

questions.prompt: Why is rebuilding an old commit weaker recovery evidence?
questions.answer: Dependencies, base tags, build tooling and build context may differ. Selecting the original tested artifact preserves the bytes you actually approved; rebuilding requires a new test and evidence chain.

questions.prompt: What did the restore comparison prove?
questions.hint: Name the fields and the snapshot boundary.
questions.answer: For the quiesced synthetic dataset, the saved logical dump restored all six task fields into a distinct database. It did not prove point-in-time recovery, external-service recovery or public identity configuration.

questions.prompt: When can image rollback make an incident worse?
questions.answer: If the old binary assumes a schema or data representation no longer present, rollback adds errors. A compatible forward fix or isolated recovery may be safer; test that decision against the actual migration history.

capstone.title: Release and recover Taskboard v0.2
capstone.scenario: A teammate must start the complete private stack from your release, verify user isolation, recover its data and return to a known-good artifact after an incorrect deployment selection.
capstone.startingPoint: Your committed Taskboard source, private generated lab configuration, pinned dependencies and the procedures above.
requirements: Document clean-checkout environment setup and all three test commands.
Record source commit, image ID, base/dependency pins, migration versions and exact test results.
Restore the saved dump into a fresh database and verify full task content.
Measure the bad-selection detection and recovery time.
Document schema rollback limits and private teaching-auth limitations.
acceptance: A fresh checkout builds without using your source mounts or existing Python venv.
Unit, real database and real HTTP checks pass against the identified candidate.
At least one incomplete and one completed task match after restore, including owner and timestamps.
Recovery selects the same tested artifact without rebuilding it.
Another person can follow the runbook and explain one limitation.

docker compose exec -T db psql -U taskboard -d "$RESTORE_DB" -c "$QUERY" > reports/week08-restored.csv || exit 1
diff -u reports/week08-source.csv reports/week08-restored.csv

runbook.expected: No differences for a nonempty stable task dataset.
runbook.troubleshoot: If writers changed the source after backup, the comparison is invalid as a snapshot-equality test. Quiesce the lab and repeat with a fresh named destination; do not dismiss unexplained differences.

hints: The database backup must survive outside the container.
Do not copy .env into Git to make a clean checkout easier.
solution: Rehearse from a new working folder with a fresh generated .env and an isolated Compose project if running alongside the original.
Run the three suites, record the candidate identity and test that candidate through HTTP.
Restore to a new database, compare content, inject the bad image selection and record a measured recovery.
Have a reviewer identify the artifact and explain why an image rollback does not undo every migration.

rubric.pass: No hidden host source mount or unrecorded dependency is required.
Distinct destination matches the stable source dataset.

rubric.evidence: Failed selection, timeline and final system checks
rubric.pass: Known-good artifact restored without rebuilding or damaging source data.

stretch: Create a small Taskfile only after you can explain every command it wraps; keep failure exit codes intact.

cleanup.code:
RESTORE_DB=$(cat reports/week08-restore-name.txt) || exit 1
python -c "import re,sys; sys.exit(0 if re.fullmatch(r'taskboard_restore_[0-9a-f]{12}', sys.argv[1]) else 1)" "$RESTORE_DB" || { printf '%s\n' 'Refused an invalid disposable restore database name.'; exit 1; }
docker compose exec -T db dropdb -U taskboard "$RESTORE_DB" || exit 1
docker compose --profile test stop
explain: Read and validate the exact disposable restore name. Only after preserving its comparison evidence, drop that separate database.
Stop the course containers while retaining the source database volume, dump and reports.
Validation uses an explicit exit code and the shell stops on failure, so a failed name check cannot fall through into a query or dropdb. It also remains active under Python optimization.
An explicit failure branch stops the sequence instead of letting later commands run after a failed prerequisite. Correct the cause and reopen Bash if the guard closed this terminal.
cleanup.expected: Only the temporary restored database is removed; the source data remains.
cleanup.troubleshoot: If the name check fails, stop. Never substitute taskboard into the cleanup command.
